_readme: Pinned ffmpeg binaries, per host triple. Read by BOTH scripts/fetch-ffmpeg.sh
(POSIX + Git Bash) and scripts/build-server.ps1 (native Windows CI) so the two
fetch paths cannot drift apart.
Why pinned: every source here used to be a 'latest' moving target with no
integrity check, so two builds of the same commit could ship different ffmpeg
binaries. Windows was worst — it pulled ffmpeg-master-latest, i.e. FFmpeg git
trunk nightlies, into shipped installers.
To upgrade: bump version + url + sha256 together. The fetchers re-download
automatically when this file changes (the .pinned stamp beside the binary is
compared against version+sha256), and abort on a hash mismatch.
MIRRORED TRIPLES (windows, linux): their `url` points at THIS repo's own
release assets, not at the upstream builder. BtbN prunes its autobuild tags
after roughly 11-15 days, which 404'd the pin mid-release on v1.8.0 and took
the Windows server build down after the freeze had already succeeded.
Re-pinning only bought another ~11 days, so the artifacts are now served by
us. The mirrored assets are BYTE-IDENTICAL copies: `sha256`, `archive`,
`member` and `bin` are unchanged from the upstream pin, which is exactly why
both fetchers needed no modification — and it makes the pre-existing sha256
double as proof that the mirror is a faithful copy rather than a re-roll.
Re-mirror with scripts/mirror-ffmpeg.sh (it refuses to upload anything whose
hash does not already match the pin), then move `url` onto the new asset.
The mirror release MUST stay a prerelease. GitHub resolves `releases/latest`
to the newest non-prerelease release, and that is the endpoint the in-app
updater polls for latest-server.json / latest-client.json. A mirror release
promoted to a normal release would become `latest`, 404 that endpoint, and
break auto-update for every already-installed build.
Rot is watched for, not just hoped against: scripts/verify-ffmpeg-pins.sh
checks every triple (reachable + sha256 + member extracts) and is run weekly
by .github/workflows/ffmpeg-pin-freshness.yml, which files an issue when a
pin breaks. Separately, both build scripts now vendor ffmpeg BEFORE the
PyInstaller freeze rather than after it, so a rotted pin fails the build in
seconds instead of 40 minutes — that ordering is the fail-fast gate, and it
is why the vendoring block sits near the top of build-server.{sh,ps1}.
Requirements every entry must keep:
- libass + libfreetype + fontconfig  -> subtitle burn-in ('subtitles' filter)
- NO --enable-nonfree                -> nonfree builds are not redistributable
- static (no non-system dylibs)      -> bundles as a single file resource
ffprobe is deliberately not vendored: nothing in the codebase invokes it.
`bin` is NOT free to rename: server_process.rs::locate_bundled_ffmpeg()
derives the same 'ffmpeg{.exe}' name from target_os independently of this
file. They agree today; changing `bin` alone would vendor a name the locator
cannot find, and burn-in would fail to locate ffmpeg at runtime.

_notes: arm64-NATIVE, so Apple Silicon needs no Rosetta. evermeet (used for the
x86_64 triple) ships x86_64 only; running that under Rosetta on arm64 was
the previous behaviour, and it fails outright on a Silicon Mac without
Rosetta — an exec'd subprocess gets EBADARCH with no install prompt, so
burn-in just silently stops working.
provenance=tofu: osxexperts publishes no checksums, so this sha256 is our
own first-fetch value (verified: arm64, static, libass, GPL, no nonfree).
Unlike the evermeet and BtbN URLs, this one is NOT version-exact — the
filename carries the major version only (8.1), so osxexperts can rebuild
8.1.x in place. A sha256 mismatch on THIS triple therefore most likely
means an upstream rebuild, not tampering: re-verify the new binary still
meets the requirements above, then re-pin. The fetchers fail closed, so a
rebuild surfaces as a hard macOS CI failure rather than a silent swap.
Version reads 8.1 while x86_64 reads 8.1.2 — the two builders publish on
their own cadences, so the mac triples are not kept in version lockstep
(unlike Windows/Linux, which share one BtbN tag).
Was https://evermeet.cx/ffmpeg/getrelease/zip — a 'latest' alias that
silently rolls. Same publisher, now pinned to the exact version URL.
provenance=tofu: evermeet publishes GPG .sig files but no sha256; this is
our own first-fetch value.
Was ffmpeg-master-latest-win64-gpl.zip from the rolling 'latest' tag —
FFmpeg git TRUNK, rebuilt daily, shipped to users. Then pinned to a dated
BtbN autobuild tag serving the 8.1.2 RELEASE branch (+32 commits).
provenance=upstream-checksums: the sha256 is BtbN's own published
checksums.sha256 value for that tag, so it is not a trust-on-first-use
value — and it still holds, because the mirror copies those exact bytes.
MIRRORED: url now serves from this repo (see the mirror section in
_readme). It was BtbN autobuild-2026-07-30-13-32; BtbN prunes autobuild
tags after ~11-15 days, and that pruning is what broke the v1.8.0 release.
A 404 here would now mean the mirror asset itself went missing, which is
a much louder and more fixable problem than an upstream retention window.
Dev-convenience triple — no Linux installer ships. Moved off johnvansickle
(which deletes older versioned tarballs, so a pinned URL there would 404)
onto the same BtbN tag as Windows, keeping both on one version.
MIRRORED alongside Windows, from the same BtbN tag, for the same reason
(see the mirror section in _readme). Keeping the two on one mirror release
preserves the single-version property that motivated the original move.
